measurements.title: Corrected Reflectance
measurements.blurb: What the satellite saw, as close to a photograph as an instrument gets — every day since 2000.

measurements.title: Earth at Night
measurements.blurb: City light, gas flares, fishing fleets and the moonlit clouds between them.

measurements.title: Geostationary
measurements.blurb: One hemisphere, every ten minutes. This is what a hurricane looks like while it turns.

measurements.title: Fires & Thermal Anomalies
measurements.blurb: Pixels hot enough to be burning, detected twice a day per satellite.

measurements.title: Land Surface Reflectance
measurements.blurb: Atmosphere removed — the ground's own colour, and false-colour bands that pull vegetation, burn scars and cities apart.

measurements.title: Blue Marble
measurements.blurb: The cloudless Earth. No date, no gaps — the reference picture.

measurements.title: Reference
measurements.blurb: Coastlines, borders and labels to hang the imagery on.

measurements.title: Aerosol Optical Depth
measurements.blurb: How much smoke, dust and haze the air column is carrying.

measurements.title: Dust
measurements.blurb: Saharan and Gobi dust, scored from infrared.

measurements.title: Surface Water Extent
measurements.blurb: Where there is water today that usually isn't — flooding, at 30 m.

measurements.title: Vegetation Disturbance
measurements.blurb: Land that has lost its cover since last year: fire, logging, drought, development.

measurements.title: Water Vapour
measurements.blurb: The invisible ocean overhead.

measurements.title: Clouds
measurements.blurb: Cloud fraction and cloud-top temperature — how much sky is covered and how high the tops are.

measurements.title: Precipitation
measurements.blurb: Rain and snow rate, merged from a constellation.

measurements.title: Air Quality
measurements.blurb: Nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide and total column ozone.

measurements.title: Land Surface Temperature
measurements.blurb: The skin temperature of the ground itself — day and night.

measurements.title: Vegetation Indices
measurements.blurb: How green the land is, and how that changes with the seasons.

measurements.title: Snow Cover
measurements.blurb: Snow on the ground, and how much water is in it.

measurements.title: Land Cover
measurements.blurb: Forest, cropland, urban, ice — classified once a year.

measurements.title: Population Density
measurements.blurb: Where people are, on the same grid as the imagery.

measurements.title: Sea Surface Temperature
measurements.blurb: Ocean skin temperature, and how far it is from normal.

measurements.title: Chlorophyll a
measurements.blurb: Where the ocean is alive — phytoplankton, blooms and currents.

measurements.title: Sea Ice
measurements.blurb: Ice concentration at both poles, daily since 2012.

measurements.title: Orbital Tracks
measurements.blurb: Where the satellite actually flew, with the time it passed.

layers.title: Corrected Reflectance (True Color)
layers.about: True Color: Red = Band 1, Green = Band 4, Blue = Band 3 These images are called true-color or natural color because this combination of wavelengths is similar to what the human eye would see. The images are natural-looking images of land surface, oceanic and atmospheric features. The downside of this set of bands is that they tend to produce a hazy image.

layers.title: Corrected Reflectance (Bands 7-2-1)
layers.about: False Color: Red = Band 7, Green = Band 2, Blue = Band 1 This combination is most useful for distinguishing burn scars from naturally low vegetation or bare soil and enhancing floods. This combination can also be used to distinguish snow and ice from clouds. Snow and ice are very reflective in the visible part of the spectrum (Band 1), and absorbent in Bands 2 (near infrared) and 7 (short-wave infrared, or SWIR).

layers.title: Corrected Reflectance (Bands 3-6-7)
layers.about: False Color: Red = Band 3, Green = Band 6, Blue = Band 7 This combination is used to map snow and ice. Snow and ice are very reflective in the visible part of the spectrum (Band 3), and very absorbent in Bands 6 and 7 (short-wave infrared, or SWIR). This band combination is good for distinguishing liquid water from frozen water, for example, clouds over snow, ice cloud versus water cloud; or floods from dense vegetation.

layers.title: Blue Marble, Shaded Relief and Bathymetry
layers.about: The MODIS Blue Marble, Next Generation layer with Shaded Relief and Bathymetry is a cloud free, true color composite of MODIS imagery from August 2004 including shaded relief and bathymetry in the water bodies.

layers.title: Blue Marble, Shaded Relief
layers.about: The MODIS Blue Marble, Next Generation layer with Shaded Relief is a cloud free, true color composite of MODIS imagery from August 2004 including shaded relief.

layers.title: Blue Marble, Next Generation

layers.title: Landsat WELD True Color (annual)
layers.sub: Landsat 7 / ETM+ — one image per year, 30 m
layers.about: The Surface Reflectance (NBAR, True Color, Global, Annual, Version 3.1) layer is a true color composite of images from all available Landsat 4 and 5 Thematic Mapper (TM) and Landsat 7 Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus (ETM+) Collection 1 data and is produced by the Global Web Enabled Landsat Data (GWELD) project. The layer is created from Landsat Band 3, 2, 1 Nadir BRDF (Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function) Adjusted Reflectance (NBAR).

layers.title: False Colour (Landsat, 30 m)
layers.about: NOTE: This layer is undergoing beta testing. The dynamically generated Reflectance (Bands 5-4-3, Color Infrared) imagery layer is a false color composite that is used to gauge plant health and assess plant density. Plants reflect in near infrared and green light, while absorbing in red. Areas with better vegetation health appear red, and denser plant growth is a darker red.

layers.title: False Colour (Sentinel-2, 30 m)
layers.about: NOTE: This layer is undergoing beta testing. The dynamically generated Reflectance (Bands 8-4-3, Color Infrared) imagery layer is a false color composite that is used to gauge plant health and assess plant density. Plants reflect in near infrared and green light, while absorbing in red. Areas with better vegetation health appear red, and denser plant growth is a darker red.

layers.title: Fires and Thermal Anomalies, 375 m (day)
layers.about: The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) Fire and Thermal Anomalies (Day, 375m) layer shows active fire detections and thermal anomalies, such as volcanoes, and gas flares. Fires can be set naturally, such as by lightning, or by humans, whether intentionally or accidentally.

layers.title: Aerosol Optical Depth (combined)
layers.about: NOTICE: There is no imagery for the period between 2022 OCT 11 and 2023 APR 25. The MODIS (Terra and Aqua) Combined Value-Added Aerosol Optical Depth layer is a value-added layer based on MODIS Level 2 aerosol products. The layer can give a quick, synoptic view of the level of aerosol in the atmosphere.

layers.title: Aerosol Optical Depth
layers.about: The Aerosol Optical Depth layer is useful for studying aerosol optical depth over the ocean as well as vegetation/dark-soiled land, which are both dark in the visible wavelengths. It is produced using two “Dark Target” (DT) algorithms for retrieving (1) over ocean (dark in visible and longer wavelengths) and (2) over vegetated/dark-soiled land (dark in the visible).

layers.title: Aerosol Optical Depth
layers.about: The Aerosol Optical Depth layer is useful for studying aerosol optical depth over the ocean as well as vegetation/dark-soiled land, which are both dark in the visible wavelengths. It is produced using two “Dark Target” (DT) algorithms for retrieving (1) over ocean (dark in visible and longer wavelengths) and (2) over vegetated/dark-soiled land (dark in the visible).

layers.title: Dust Score (day)
layers.about: Description Dust score is determined from multiple tests that compare radiances in select AIRS spectral channels. Radiances measured in channels that are sensitive to dust are compared to radiances measured in channels that are not sensitive to dust. The differences between several pairs of channels are represented as a dust score. Higher scores indicate more certainty that dust is present. Dust is probable when the score is above 380.

layers.title: Dust Score (night)
layers.about: Description Dust score is determined from multiple tests that compare radiances in select AIRS spectral channels. Radiances measured in channels that are sensitive to dust are compared to radiances measured in channels that are not sensitive to dust. The differences between several pairs of channels are represented as a dust score. Higher scores indicate more certainty that dust is present. Dust is probable when the score is above 380.

layers.title: Dust RGB
layers.about: Note: This layer is generally available for the most recent 90 days, though certain historical ranges are also preserved.

layers.title: Dynamic Surface Water Extent (30 m)
layers.about: The OPERA Dynamic Surface Water Extent imagery layer is a Level-3 (L3) product that maps surface water every few days. The resolution is 30 m and the layer has 5 classifications: Not Water, Open Water, Partial Surface Water, Snow/Ice, and Cloud/Cloud Shadow.

layers.title: Vegetation Disturbance Alert (30 m)
layers.about: The OPERA Land Surface Disturbance (DIST-ALERT) imagery layer is a Level-3 (L3) product that maps per pixel vegetation disturbance (specifically, vegetation cover loss). Vegetation disturbance is mapped when there is an indicated decrease in vegetation cover within an HLS pixel. The spatial resolution is 30 m and the displayed layer describes vegetation disturbance status based on confidence, magnitude of loss, and whether it is ongoing.

layers.title: Water Vapour (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Precipitable Water Vapor layer shows the total amount of water vapor in a 5 km by 5 km column of the atmosphere, measured in centimeters (cm). Water cycles through the Earth’s atmosphere in three states: solid (ice), liquid (rain drops), gas (water vapor). Water vapor is the gaseous form of water, which occurs when water gets hotter and it changes from a liquid to a gas.

layers.title: Water Vapour (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Precipitable Water Vapor layer shows the total amount of water vapor in a 5 km by 5 km column of the atmosphere, measured in centimeters (cm). Water cycles through the Earth’s atmosphere in three states: solid (ice), liquid (rain drops), gas (water vapor). Water vapor is the gaseous form of water, which occurs when water gets hotter and it changes from a liquid to a gas.

layers.title: Cloud Fraction (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Cloud Fraction is a measure of the percentage of Earth’s surface covered by clouds. Cloud Fraction is important in determining the amount of sunlight that reaches the Earth’s surface, the amount of sunlight reflected back into space, and the amount of heat escaping from the surface and atmosphere back into space. Clouds play a very important role in the Earth’s energy budget and climate system.

layers.title: Cloud Top Temperature (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Cloud Top Temperature (Day) layer indicates the atmospheric temperature at the top of the clouds measured in Kelvin (K). Clouds play an important role in the radiative balance of the Earth. Clouds can contain ice or water and each will react differently.

layers.title: Precipitation Rate
layers.about: The IMERG Precipitation Rate layer displays rain rate and snow rate in millimeters per hour (mm/hr). It is estimated by the Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) (IMERG) algorithm.

layers.title: Precipitation Rate (ascending)
layers.about: The Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Microwave Imager (GMI) Precipitation Rate (Ascending) layer provides the rate at which rain and frozen precipitation (snow) reaches the Earth's surface in millimeters per hour (mm/hr). The layer shows both the Rain Rate and Snow Rate with two different legends. This layer provides snapshots of individual storms, including tropical cyclones and flood-producing systems.

layers.title: Nitrogen Dioxide (tropospheric column)
layers.about: The OMI Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) tropospheric parameter displays the tropospheric component of the total NO2 column measured in molecules/cm<sup2</sup.

layers.title: Ozone (total column)
layers.about: The OMPS Ozone layer indicates the amount of ozone in the total column and is measured in Dobson Units (DU).

layers.title: Carbon Monoxide at 500 hPa (day)
layers.about: The Carbon Monoxide (L3, 500hPa, Day, Daily) layer displays carbon monoxide in units of parts per billion by volume at the 500 hPa pressure level, approximately 5500 meters (18,000 feet) above sea level.

layers.title: Land Surface Temperature (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Land Surface Temperature (Day) layer shows the temperature of the land surface in Kelvin (K).

layers.title: Land Surface Temperature (night)
layers.about: The MODIS Land Surface Temperature (Night) layer shows the temperature of the land surface in Kelvin (K).

layers.title: Land Surface Temperature (day)
layers.about: The MODIS Land Surface Temperature (Day) layer shows the temperature of the land surface in Kelvin (K).

layers.title: Vegetation Index, NDVI (8-day)
layers.about: The MODIS Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) layer is a measure of the greenness and health of vegetation. The index is calculated based on how much red and near-infrared light is reflected by plant leaves. The index values range from -0.2 to 1 where higher values (0.3 to 1) indicate areas covered by green, leafy vegetation and lower values (0 to 0.3) indicate areas where there is little or no vegetation.

layers.title: Vegetation Index, NDVI (monthly)
layers.about: The Vegetation Index (L3, Monthly) layer is created from the Terra Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Vegetation Indices (MOD13A3) data which are provided monthly at 1 kilometer (km) spatial resolution as a gridded Level 3 product in the sinusoidal projection. In generating this monthly product, the algorithm ingests all the Terra MODIS Vegetation Indices 16-day products that overlap the month and employs a weighted temporal average.

layers.title: Vegetation Index, NDVI (30 m)
layers.about: NOTE: This layer is undergoing beta testing. The dynamically generated Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) imagery layer is an index for quantifying green vegetation. NDVI is used to quantify vegetation greenness, understand vegetation density and monitor plant health. In healthy vegetation, chlorophyll strongly absorbs visible light while the structure of leaves strongly reflects near infrared light.

layers.title: Snow Cover (NDSI)
layers.about: The MODIS Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI) snow cover layer shows the presence of snow cover over land and water bodies as an index related to the presence of snow. NDSI snow cover is derived from the cloud free snow reflectance sensed by the MODIS instrument, and hence this layer shows presence of snow during day time and under cloud clear condition only.

layers.title: Snow Cover (NDSI)
layers.about: The MODIS Snow Cover (Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI)) layer shows the presence of snow cover over land and water bodies as an index related to the presence of snow. NDSI snow cover is derived from the cloud free snow reflectance sensed by the MODIS instrument, and hence this layer shows presence of snow during day time and under cloud clear condition only.

layers.title: Snow Water Equivalent
layers.about: The Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer-E/Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer-2 (AMSR-E/AMSR2) “Snow Water Equivalent” (SWE) layer displays daily SWE estimates in millimeters (mm) for the Northern Hemisphere rendered to an azimuthal 25 km Equal-Area Scalable Earth Grid (EASE-Grid).

layers.title: Land Cover Type (IGBP, annual)
layers.about: The Terra and Aqua combined Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Land Cover Type (MCD12Q1) Version 6.1 data product provides global land cover types at yearly intervals. The MCD12Q1 Version 6.1 data product is derived using supervised classifications of MODIS Terra and Aqua reflectance data.

layers.title: Population Density (2020)
layers.about: The Population Density, 2020 layer is from the Gridded Population of the World, Version 4 (GPWv4) Population Count Adjusted to Match 2015 Revision of UN WPP Country Totals. It consists of estimates of human population consistent with national censuses and population registers with respect to relative spatial distribution, but adjusted to match 2015 Revision of UN World Population Prospects country totals for the years 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, and 2020.

layers.title: Sea Surface Temperature
layers.about: The Sea Surface Temperature (L4, MUR) layer is created from the GHRSST Sea Surface Temperature Level 4, MUR sea surface temperature analysis product, which uses wavelets as basis functions in an optimal interpolation approach on a global 0.011 degree grid.

layers.title: Sea Surface Temperature Anomalies
layers.sub: MUR — difference from the seasonal normal
layers.about: The Sea Surface Temperature Anomalies (L4, MUR) layer is created from the GHRSST Sea Surface Temperature Level 4, MUR sea surface temperature analysis product, which uses wavelets as basis functions in an optimal interpolation approach on a global 0.011 degree grid.

layers.title: Sea Surface Temperature (AVHRR OI)
layers.about: The Sea Surface Temperature (L4) layer is a Group for High Resolution Sea Surface Temperature (GHRSST) global Level 4 sea surface temperature analysis, produced daily on a 0.25 degree grid at the NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. This product uses optimal interpolation (OI) by interpolating and extrapolating SST observations from different sources, resulting in a smoothed complete field.

layers.title: Chlorophyll a
layers.about: The MODIS Chlorophyll a layer provides the near-surface concentration of chlorophyll a in milligrams of chlorophyll pigment per cubic meter (mg/m<sup3</sup) in the ocean.

layers.title: Chlorophyll a
layers.about: The VIIRS Chlorophyll a layer provides the near-surface concentration of chlorophyll a in milligrams of chlorophyll pigment per cubic meter (mg/m<sup3</sup) in the ocean.

layers.title: Chlorophyll a
layers.about: The Chlorophyll a layer provides the near-surface concentration of chlorophyll a in milligrams of chlorophyll pigment per cubic meter (mg/m<sup3</sup) in the ocean.

layers.title: Sea Ice Concentration (12 km)
layers.about: The Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer-E/Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer-2 (AMSR-E/AMSR2) unified “Sea Ice Concentration (12 km)” layer displays the percent of sea ice concentration in the polar regions as a daily composite of the AMSR2 1:30 a.m. ascending and 1:30 p.m. descending half-orbit passes, at a spatial resolution of 12 km.

layers.title: Sea Ice Concentration (25 km)
layers.about: The Sea Ice Concentration (L4, MUR25) layer is a Group for High Resolution Sea Surface Temperature (GHRSST) Level 4 sea surface temperature analysis. It is produced as a retrospective dataset (four day latency) and near-real-time dataset (one day latency) at the JPL Physical Oceanography DAAC using wavelets as basis functions in an optimal interpolation approach on a global 0.25 degree grid.

layers.title: Coastlines
layers.about: The Coastlines layer is a reference layer that displays global coastlines. Coastlines information are gleaned from OpenStreetMap and the SCAR Antarctic Digital Database (2010) for Antarctic coastlines.

layers.title: Borders and Roads
layers.about: The Coastlines/Borders/Roads layer is a reference layer that displays global coastlines, country borders, first order administrative boundaries and major roads.

layers.title: Place Labels
layers.about: The Place Labels layer is a reference layer that displays labels for countries, states, major cities, minor cities, towns, airports, universities/schools, hospitals, water bodies, and national parks/protected areas.

layers.title: Orbital Track, Aqua (ascending)
layers.about: The Aqua - Orbit Track & Time (Ascending/Day) layer is the path of the Aqua satellite on its ascending/day-time orbit. Overpass times are shown in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Local overpass time at the equator has drifted to ~14:30 as the satellite has reached end-of-life and is continuing to drift.

layers.title: Orbital Track, Terra (descending)
layers.about: The Terra Orbital Track & Overpass Time (Descending/Day) layer is the path of the Terra satellite on its descending/day-time orbit. Overpass times are shown in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Local overpass time at the equator has drifted to ~09:30 as the satellite has reached end-of-life and is continuing to drift.

layers.title: Orbital Track, Suomi NPP (ascending)
layers.about: The Suomi NPP Orbital Track & Overpass Time (Ascending/Day) layer is the path of the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (Suomi NPP) satellite on its ascending/day-time orbit. Overpass times are shown in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Local overpass time at the equator is approximately 13:30.
